target_customer: Migraine patients, with employers as a stated secondary payer in the seed announcement
problem: Migraine patients cycle through medications by trial and error. Mable used a cheek swab pharmacogenetic test plus telehealth to pick the drug and dose, with ongoing clinician follow up.
business_model: Direct to consumer telehealth clinic with genetic testing and prescriptions; employer benefit angle mentioned

founders.name: Roman Rothaermel
founders.background_notes: Neuroscientist with research on memory encoding, neuropharmacology and drug target characterization, per the YC page.

founders.name: Inna Thalmann
education: University of Oxford, PhD in econometrics with a health economics focus
founders.background_notes: Postdoctoral work on phenotype algorithms for cheaper clinical trials, per the YC page.

competitors.name: Cove
competitors.what: Telemedicine startup for migraine sufferers, prescribing migraine medication online, founded by former Google employees

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed a pharmacogenetic testing pipeline, clinical protocols and prescribing across jurisdictions, but built on existing lab and telehealth components.

defensibility.rationale: Clinical protocols and lab partnerships took effort, but other telehealth migraine clinics could add a genetic test.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No public record found of incumbents copying or buying it.

market_need_then: The seed announcement cites migraines costing US employers about 13 billion dollars a year per the Initialized post; many patients lack effective personalized treatment.

branding.domain_note: Used trymable.com rather than mable.com; trymable.com now redirects to an unrelated hair site.

identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical outcome claims such as 55 percent pain reduction

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself; mostly funding coverage. The legal entity is Neurolytic Healthcare and the name is shared with other companies.

outcome_analysis: Mable raised a 3.2 million dollar seed in July 2022 led by Initialized, then appears to have wound down: a directory reports the UK entity was dissolved in August 2023 while YC lists it as acquired with no named buyer. The cause is not public. Failure to raise a follow on round in the 2022 to 2023 funding downturn is a plausible but unconfirmed reading, so it is tagged with low certainty.
notes: YC status is Acquired but no acquirer found; one directory (healthcarediscovery.ai) says it wound down by August 2023 and the UK entity dissolved 2023-08-08. Exit type left unknown because the sources conflict. Neura Health (founded 2020 per Owler, unverified) and Migrevention are other migraine startups but were not verified as of 2021. Seed amount shown as 3M in Axios headline and 3.2M in other outlets; 3.2M used. The failure factor is an inference, cause not public.
